sources.citation: real-world (product class), makers' listings seen in search summaries, 2026-11-18, not read in full: medium-base (E26) porcelain lampholders that mount on an outlet box, keyless and pull-chain, are marked 660 W at 250 V on makers' and distributors' listings; lampholders are listed to UL 496 (cited by number). The simulator reads neither value; the inspector may.

game-design inside a read class: a porcelain base drawn 108 × 108 mm (4-1/4 in, enough to cover a 4 in outlet box; the listings read mount on 4 in and 3-1/4 in boxes) and 64 mm tall with the socket; top-wired (screws on the back face, toward the box), brass (hot) and silver (neutral) either side of the socket and a green grounding screw below. Not every product in the class has a grounding screw; the kind gives every lampholder one.

real-world for the contacts, game-design for the place: the socket's screw shell is the grounded conductor's and its centre contact the ungrounded one's (NFPA 70-2023 Art. 200.10(C), screw shells, cited by number), so the shell is on the silver screw and the centre contact on the brass one (through the pull-chain switch on that holder). The E26 socket is on the base's axis with its bottom 40 mm above the back face (game-design).

game-design anchored to a published figure: one lampholder maker's product pages give a terminal-screw torque range of 14 to 18 lb·in (1.6 to 2.0 N·m) (read 2026-11-12 for the P3 lamp holder, paraphrased, the maker not named). The fictional holder is marked 1.8 N·m (about 16 lb·in), inside it; NFPA 70-2023 Art. 110.14(D) requires the marked value (cited by number). No UL 486A-B torque table is used.

game-design inside a read class: the holder's binding-head screws take one copper conductor each, 14 or 12 AWG, solid or stranded, wrapped clockwise under the head; not marked for aluminium. One pull-chain holder listing seen in a search summary (2026-11-18) gives 14 to 10 AWG; 14 to 12 is used, as on the P3 holder. Stranded copper under a binding head splays (ADR 0018 §4.3). The 16 ± 3 mm strip wraps about three-quarters of a turn round the screw and the head grips 12 mm of it (not published figures).
game-design: conductors come from the box behind the holder and reach each screw on its back face along -z; not modelled on a product.

game-design: a slotted and Phillips combination head on every terminal screw, the green grounding screw included, common on wiring-device terminal screws (common practice, not one product); the drive type is a name and its size is not modelled.

NBS Building Science Series 103 (W. J. Meese and R. W. Beausoliel, 1977; read in the P3 source pre-audit, ADR 0018 §4.1): good branch-circuit wiring-device screw-terminal connections dropped 3 to 8 mV at 15 A, 0.2 to 0.5 mΩ. The class value 0.3 mΩ is taken as R₀, the contact resistance at the marked torque with a copper conductor at 20 °C; the engine scales it for torque, strip length, conductor count, strand spread and nicks (ADR 0018 §4).

game-design calibration (ADR 0018 §3.3, §11), the screw-terminal class's values, as on the P3 lamp holder: the heat path into the device, 0.026 W/K, is calibrated, not measured (with 14 AWG copper at 15 A it puts BSS 103's 18 to 36 W glowing connections between the Draper point, about 525 °C, and about 1000 °C). The clamp's heat capacity, 1.1 J/K, is a physics estimate: about 3 g of brass screw and terminal plate × about 380 J/(kg·K).
